Evidence: [checkpoint-artifacts.ts:30](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rl/blob/6de2805236f0d955cb49a476c4f5e8cdfd510a9a/checkpoint-artifacts.ts#L30), [src/blobs.ts:12](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-rlm/blob/64d70bdc023db07be5973aaed19a96178b22554d/src/blobs.ts#L12), [engine/objects.ts:235](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/a8afb1a283c1beac6cd8db1ffd1ef5a13c5196f8/engine/objects.ts#L235).

Problem: at least three packages own digest addressing, immutable put/get verification, root manifests/reachability and artifact retention. The SDK provides atomic file writes, tracker locks and tracker workspace snapshots; it does not export a generic immutable blob repository with backend-neutral storage. A tracker snapshot is not an arbitrary payload blob. Draft API: a namespaced adapter with put(bytes), getVerified(digest), immutable references, bounded regular-file IO, caller-owned publication locks and explicit roots/GC dry-run receipts. Keep VCS framing, erasure denials/signatures and RL retention policy in their packages. Acceptance: equal bytes share identity, mismatched stored bytes fail closed, concurrent same-digest publication is idempotent, lost-lease publication is refused, GC never retires referenced blobs, and a non-filesystem adapter passes the same contract. No hosted backend support should be claimed until tested.


Source: a read-only audit of 30 fleet extensions against the exported SDK of @unbrained/pm-cli 2026.10.23 (3,188 exported names); each of the three cited packages re-implements this primitive today.
GH-1565: provide an immutable content-addressed artifact primitive for extensions
External report: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1565. Revalidate the reported 2026.10.23 behavior against the checkout before implementation.
Specify a backend-neutral immutable artifact contract with verified digests and bounded IO; prove concurrent publication and referenced-root retention; preserve package-specific framing and policy

patch.value: Extensions can share a backend-neutral immutable artifact primitive with verified digests; safe concurrent publication and root-aware retention are independently proven.
